newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks fall 2.66 pct by lunch, finance sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks fall 2.66 pct by lunch, finance sales.

text.p: Worries over the future of financial institutions along with a lack of confidence prompted investors to sell stocks across the board and drove the index down 2.66 percent by lunch break on Wednesday, brokers said.
The composite SET index lost 17.28 points to 631.19 on thin 1.4 billion baht turnover by the lunch break.

"Investors didn't have confidence in the market as they're not sure whether the central bank and the finance ministry would in the near-term suspend more finance companies or not," said a broker at a foreign house.
Brokers said investor's concerns came after the government on Tuesday suspended 42 finance firms, bringing to a total of 58 finance companies suspended since June.
To date there are 33 finance companies and 15 commercial banks which are considered healthy by authorities.
"There's no guarantee that there won't be closure of finance firms in future," said the broker at foreign brokerage.
"Foreigners were active before the announcement came out (on Tuesday). They stayed on the sidelines this morning because they also did not have full confidence in the market," said the broker.
Brokers said investors were also worried that fees on public utilities like electricity, telephone and water would rise following a three percentage point hike in the value added tax.

The finance sector was the most active in terms of value, losing 3.73 percent. Dhana Siam Finance topped the active list, declining 3.25 baht to 32.75. -- Suthep Chawla (662) 652-0642, email: bangkok.newsroom@reuters.com
